answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 256GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes achieve consensus while 1,000 fakes stall, failing to return the wharf of a valid computational state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting random data indices; failure to return data matching the isolated island of the working set triggers an immediate penalty. This garden of memory latency ensures each agent keeps unique bus access to prevent pooling. Honest participants pay 60 watts to maintain their status, while 1,000 fakes incur 60,000 watts.
